title: Longnail: High-Level Synthesis of Portable Custom Instruction Set Extensions for RISC-V Processors from Descriptions in the Open-Source CoreDSL Language
problem: Exploring different combinations of base RISC-V cores and custom instruction set extensions (ISAXes) for specific applications requires automation and portability across microarchitectures, which existing approaches do not provide. Current ISA extension design workflows lack the ability to efficiently explore and compare design choices across heterogeneous microarchitectures.
motivation: Custom instruction set extensions are energy-efficient and cost-effective methods for accelerating embedded workloads in RISC-V processors, but their design and exploration requires systematic automation.
method: Longnail automates the creation of custom processor instructions for RISC-V. You describe the instructions you want in CoreDSL, a specialized language, and Longnail generates the hardware needed to add them to any RISC-V processor. Because it automatically handles the differences between different RISC-V cores, one CoreDSL description works across all of them, letting you quickly explore and compare different processor configurations.
key_novelty: One CoreDSL description automatically generates custom RISC-V instruction extensions for any processor core, so you can explore different hardware designs without rewriting the specification each time.
contributions: Longnail framework for automated synthesis of portable RISC-V instruction set extensions
CoreDSL language integration for high-level descriptions of custom instructions
Support for systematic exploration of base core and ISAX combinations
Portability across different RISC-V microarchitectures without redesign
primary_theme: Portable ISA extension synthesis for RISC-V
